changes: v1.0.0 — first public build (PLAN-2026-10-06 §1): ONE self-contained HTML page carrying both digest streams as AES-256-GCM ciphertext. Public bytes = ciphertext + static code only; PBKDF2-SHA256 (600,000 iterations, 16-byte salt, 12-byte IV, AAD-bound params) derives the AES-256 key in the browser and the page decrypts + renders client-side. No build step, no packages, no network call carries the passphrase.

v1.0.0 — noindex meta; the site robots.txt already disallows everything. noindex is etiquette, not secrecy.

The gate is real for realistic leak shapes; the defence for the bare shape is that the passphrase never enters this repo.

caveat: HONEST CAVEAT: the ciphertext is public and offline-brute-forceable — passphrase strength IS the security. Git history retains old ciphertext blobs, so rotation means a new passphrase and the old blobs stay decryptable by the old passphrase (they are never rewritten). The passphrase lives outside this repo and outside every receipt; it was never printed, committed or pushed.
